# Mytetz

> Mytetz is a learning app. A reader picks a topic from a curated catalogue and studies it in a focused, guided reader.

The catalogue lists topics by title, category, and summary. A reader can search and filter the catalogue, then start a session that opens the topic in the reader.

## Pages

- [Catalogue](https://mytetz.com/): the curated list of topics, and the site's home page.
- [How it works](https://mytetz.com/how-it-works): which model writes an explanation, the known limits, and a contact.
- [Privacy policy](https://mytetz.com/privacy)
- [Terms of service](https://mytetz.com/terms)
- [Imprint](https://mytetz.com/imprint)

## Guides

Editorial pages about self-study. Every claim names a primary source, with the year and the sample size.

- [Study guides](https://mytetz.com/guides): the index of the six guides below.
- [How to study on your own](https://mytetz.com/guides/how-to-study-on-your-own): a six-step loop, built on practice testing and distributed practice.
- [What to use instead of a highlighter](https://mytetz.com/guides/what-to-use-instead-of-a-highlighter): why a 2013 review rated highlighting as low utility, and four replacements.
- [How to test yourself while you read](https://mytetz.com/guides/how-to-test-yourself-while-you-read): active recall with no flashcard deck.
- [When to review what you read](https://mytetz.com/guides/when-to-review-what-you-read): the forgetting curve, and a spaced review schedule.
- [How students study now](https://mytetz.com/guides/how-students-study-now): the 2026 survey data on study and AI, with each sample size.
- [Why a person stops an online course](https://mytetz.com/guides/why-a-person-stops-an-online-course): what the 2013-2018 completion data counts.
